n0da450d9bf5.s: After completing the normal term of five years, a Governor continues in office until:
o: The State Legislature passes a resolution
The next general election to the Assembly
n0da450d9bf5.x: The normal term is five years, but the Governor continues in office until the successor enters office.

n2e9036271c7.s: Which of the following is a proper ground for invoking Article 356?
o: An intra-party dispute in the ruling party
An ordinary law and order problem
n2e9036271c7.x: Flagrant defiance of constitutional directions is a proper ground; intra-party disputes, maladministration alone and ordinary law and order are improper.

nf09897dc339.s: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) on Centre-State relations was constituted by the:
nf09897dc339.x: The Tamil Nadu Government set up the Rajamannar Committee in 1969; its recommendations were never implemented by the Centre.

nindian-polity-10-1.s: Who is the real executive head of a State?
o: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
nindian-polity-10-1.x: The Chief Minister is the real executive head and heads the Council of Ministers; the Governor is the nominal or constitutional head.

nindian-polity-1-43.s: Who became the first woman Judge of the Supreme Court in 1989?
nindian-polity-1-43.x: Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman Supreme Court Judge in 1989 and was also the first Muslim woman in the higher judiciary.

nindian-polity-11-5.s: The oath of office to the Governor of a State is administered by the:
o: Chief Justice of the concerned High Court
nindian-polity-11-5.x: Under Article 159, the Governor's oath is administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.

nindian-polity-45-9.s: Under the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, the President may return the advice of the Council of Ministers for reconsideration:
nindian-polity-45-9.x: The 44th Amendment lets the President return ministerial advice once for reconsideration; the advice binds after that.

nindian-polity-10-8.s: If a no-confidence motion is passed in the State Legislative Assembly, who must resign?
o: The entire Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister
nindian-polity-10-8.x: The State ministry is collectively responsible to the Assembly (Art. 164(2)), so a passed no-confidence motion forces the whole ministry, CM included, to resign.

nindian-polity-11-20.s: Until 1965, the head of State of Jammu and Kashmir was called:
nindian-polity-11-20.x: The head of State of Jammu and Kashmir was called Sadr-e-Riyasat until 1965, when the title became Governor.

n18aa2baea22.s: Under Article 163(2), the Governor's decision on whether a matter falls within his discretion is:
o: Subject to approval by the Council of Ministers
Subject to approval by the President
Final, but not completely immune from judicial review
n18aa2baea22.x: Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision final on whether a matter is discretionary, but it does not create complete immunity from judicial review.

n8d50ca5d235.s: According to S.R. Bommai, the majority support of a State ministry must ordinarily be tested:
o: On the floor of the Legislative Assembly
In Raj Bhavan by the Governor
Through a report of the State Election Commission
n8d50ca5d235.x: S.R. Bommai held that majority must ordinarily be tested on the floor of the House, not in Raj Bhavan.

n6e43a5e1ae8.s: If a Bill returned by the Governor is passed again by the State Legislature, the Governor:
o: Must reserve it for the President
n6e43a5e1ae8.x: If the Legislature re-passes a Bill returned for reconsideration, the Governor must assent and cannot withhold assent again.

n1e1ab18e63c.s: Which decision prescribed timelines for the Governor and recognised deemed assent to State Bills?
o: State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor (2023)
State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu (8 April 2025)
n1e1ab18e63c.x: The 8 April 2025 ruling prescribed timelines and recognised deemed assent; the November 2025 Reference opinion rejected rigid deadlines and deemed assent.

n497bf09985a.s: A Governor addresses his resignation to the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n497bf09985a.x: A Governor resigns to the President; he may also be transferred and reappointed.

n9315a4c3060.s: The President's ordinance-making power extends to matters in the:
o: State List and the Concurrent List
Union List and the Concurrent List
n9315a4c3060.x: The President's ordinance power is co-extensive with Parliament's legislative power, including the Concurrent List.

na4e26cabba2.s: A State Bill on taxes on water or electricity in inter-State river projects is reserved for the President under Article:
na4e26cabba2.x: Taxes on water/electricity in inter-State river projects fall under Article 288; Article 304(b) concerns restrictions on inter-State trade.

nf450eb3c342.s: How many Deputy Chief Ministers did the 2019-24 Andhra Pradesh government have?
nf450eb3c342.x: The 2019-24 Andhra Pradesh government had five Deputy CMs; the Deputy CM is not a constitutional post.

nindian-polity-50-22.s: Under Article 356, the President may impose President's Rule in a State:
o: Only on the report of the Governor
Only on a resolution of the State Legislative Assembly
Only on the advice of the Chief Minister
On the report of the Governor or otherwise
nindian-polity-50-22.x: Under Article 356 the President acts on the Governor's report or otherwise when the State cannot be governed according to the Constitution.

n15191a8588e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about appointing a Chief Minister in a hung Assembly?
o: The Constitution lays down detailed criteria for the Governor's choice
The Governor may exercise discretion in selecting the Chief Minister
An early floor test is ordinarily used to establish majority support
A pre-poll alliance gets the first preference under Sarkaria and Punchhi
n15191a8588e.x: The Constitution gives no detailed criteria for a hung Assembly; the Governor uses discretion, followed by an early floor test.

n8bd88fe0ed9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 164(4) – Non-member may be a minister for twelve months
Article 164(5) – Salaries of ministers fixed by Parliament
Article 164(3) – Oath of ministers administered by the Governor
Article 164(2) – Collective responsibility to the Legislative Council
n8bd88fe0ed9.x: The Governor administers the oath under Art. 164(3). A non-member can be a minister for six months (164(4)), salaries are fixed by the State Legislature (164(5)), and responsibility is to the Assembly (164(2)).

n59723214fd2.s: In a State Legislative Council, one-third of the members retire:
n59723214fd2.x: The Legislative Council is a permanent House; one-third of its members retire every second year, each member having a six-year term.

ndd39d7e8a40.s: When a State Legislative Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker continues in office until:
o: Just before the first meeting of the new Assembly
The announcement of the election results
The Governor appoints a pro tem Speaker
ndd39d7e8a40.x: On dissolution, the Speaker does not vacate office and continues until just before the new Assembly first meets.

n212f6a264d2.s: Which of the following pairs relating to a State Money Bill is correctly matched?
o: Power of the Council over it – Rejection
Period for the Council to return it – 14 days
n212f6a264d2.x: A Money Bill is introduced only in the Assembly on the Governor's recommendation; the Council can only recommend changes within 14 days and cannot reject it.

nindian-polity-21-10.s: The maximum total period for which a Legislative Council can delay an ordinary Bill passed by the Assembly is:
nindian-polity-21-10.x: The Council can delay an ordinary Bill for at most four months (three, then one); 14 days applies to a Money Bill.

nindian-polity-40-10.s: Which of the following is a permanent body not subject to dissolution?
o: Both Houses of the State Legislature
nindian-polity-40-10.x: The Legislative Council is the permanent House, with one-third retiring every two years; the Assembly has a five-year term and can be dissolved.

nindian-polity-40-4.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 164(4) – Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers
Article 164(2) – Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Assembly
nindian-polity-40-4.x: Article 164(2) makes the State Council of Ministers collectively answerable to the Legislative Assembly; 164(3) is the oath and 164(5) the salaries.

nbe54e39e350.s: In a bicameral State Legislature, demands for grants are voted by the:
nbe54e39e350.x: The Legislative Assembly alone votes on demands for grants; the Council may discuss them but cannot vote.

nindian-polity-62-14.s: Which of the following is a field for nomination by the Governor to the State Legislative Council?
nindian-polity-62-14.x: The valid fields are literature, science, art, the co-operative movement and social service; industrial activity is not one.

nindian-polity-39-7.s: Which State has the largest Legislative Council?
nindian-polity-39-7.x: Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Council (100 members); Sikkim has no Council.

n48a6495bf7b.s: Registered graduates elect what fraction of the members of a State Legislative Council?
n48a6495bf7b.x: Registered graduates elect one-twelfth; the one-sixth share is nominated by the Governor.

n9b108f3375b.s: In the creation or abolition of a Legislative Council under Article 169, the Governor:
o: Must approve the resolution before it goes to Parliament
Can abolish the Council by notification
Has no role in initiating or approving the resolution
n9b108f3375b.x: The process starts with a special-majority resolution of the Assembly and ends with a law of Parliament; the Governor has no role in it.

n0137b8e1e71.s: The Governor addresses the State Legislature, followed by discussion, on the first day of:
o: The first session of each year
The last session of each year
n0137b8e1e71.x: The Governor addresses the Legislature on the first day of the first session of each year, and the address is followed by discussion.

nindian-polity-60-37.s: Which of the following is a ground of disqualification under Article 191?
o: Absence from the House for 60 days without permission
Ceasing to be a citizen of India
Election to both Houses of the State Legislature
nindian-polity-60-37.x: Loss of citizenship is an Article 191 ground, along with office of profit, unsound mind and insolvency; the others lead to vacation of seats under Article 190.

n8c20f49bc2b.s: Compared with the Rajya Sabha, the power of a State Legislative Council over an ordinary Bill is:
o: Equal to that of the Rajya Sabha
A power to dissolve the Assembly in a deadlock
Essentially a delaying power, and weaker
n8c20f49bc2b.x: Written as a one-liner (no dates for a sequence). The Council can only delay an Assembly Bill and cannot veto it; it is much weaker than the Rajya Sabha.

new.s: As administrator of an adjoining Union Territory, the Governor acts under Article:
new.x: Under Article 239(2), a Governor appointed administrator of an adjoining UT acts independently of his State Council of Ministers.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT appointed by the Governor of a State?
o: The Chairman of the State Public Service Commission
new.x: The President, not the Governor, appoints High Court judges; the Governor appoints the Advocate-General (165), SPSC members (316) and the State Election Commissioner (243K).

new.s: The emoluments of a Governor are charged on the:
new.x: Under Article 202(3), the Governor's emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.

new.s: The Chairman of a State Public Service Commission is appointed by the Governor but can be removed only by the:
new.x: The Governor appoints SPSC members under Article 316, but only the President can remove them.

new.s: The President's pardoning power under Article 72, unlike the Governor's under Article 161, extends to:
o: Offences against Concurrent List laws only
Cases decided by a High Court only
new.x: Article 72 covers all cases, while the Governor's power under Article 161 is limited to offences against State laws.

new.s: In Shamsher Singh (1974), a Governor's public criticism of Cabinet policy was described as:
new.x: The seven-judge bench held the Governor bound by aid and advice and called public criticism of Cabinet policy an unconstitutional faux pas.

new.s: The first dismissal of an elected State government under Article 356 took place in:
new.x: President's Rule was first imposed in Punjab in 1951, but the first elected government dismissed was Kerala's in 1959.

new.s: Which of the following States has never been under President's Rule?
new.x: Telangana and Chhattisgarh have never been under President's Rule; Manipur has had it most often.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about President's Rule in the Telugu region?
o: The 1984 Nadendla episode was a spell of President's Rule
Andhra State was under it in 1954-55
Andhra Pradesh first came under it in 1973 (Jai Andhra)
Undivided Andhra Pradesh was under it twice as of 2004
new.x: The 1984 Nadendla episode was not President's Rule; Andhra Pradesh's first spell was in 1973.

new.s: In April 2025, the Supreme Court granted deemed assent to ten Tamil Nadu Bills under Article:
new.x: The 8 April 2025 ruling used Article 142 to grant deemed assent; the Article 143 Reference of November 2025 rejected deemed assent.

new.s: Who was the first woman Chief Minister of an Indian State?
new.x: Sucheta Kripalani became the first woman CM (Uttar Pradesh, 1963); Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor.

new.s: The reservation of State Bills for the consideration of the President is an example of:
new.x: Reservation of Bills by the Governor for the President is a classic example of central control over the States.

new.s: Who has been the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh since June 2024?
new.x: N. Chandrababu Naidu became CM in June 2024; S. Abdul Nazeer is the Governor and K. Pawan Kalyan the Deputy CM.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh High Court's 2020 observation of a 'constitutional breakdown' in the State was:
new.x: The AP High Court's 2020 'constitutional breakdown' observation was stayed by the Supreme Court.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Punchhi Commission:
1. It recommended a fixed tenure for Governors.
2. It was set up in 2007 and reported in 2010.
3. It recommended that the Governor be appointed by a committee including the Lok Sabha Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Punchhi (2007-2010) recommended a fixed tenure; the appointment committee including the Lok Sabha Speaker was the NCRWC (Venkatachaliah) proposal.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 243K – Appointment of the State Election Commissioner
Article 233 – Appointment of High Court judges
new.x: Article 243K is correct. Article 176 (not 175) is the mandatory address, Article 192 excludes anti-defection, and Article 233 covers District Judges.

new.s: The cap of 15% of the Assembly's strength on the size of a State Council of Ministers was introduced by the:
new.x: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 (not 2001) fixed the 15% cap, including the CM, in Article 164(1A).

new.s: The minimum number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a State Council of Ministers is:
new.x: Article 164(1A), added by the 91st Amendment, 2003, sets a minimum of 12 ministers including the CM.

new.s: A Minister for Tribal Welfare is compulsory under Article 164(1) in:
o: Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
new.x: The four States are Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha; Bihar was dropped in 2006.

new.s: Bihar was dropped from the list of States requiring a Tribal Welfare Minister by the:
new.x: The 94th Amendment, 2006 removed Bihar from the Article 164(1) list.

new.s: Who was the Deputy Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh in 1956?
new.x: K.V. Ranga Reddy was Deputy CM of united AP in 1956, when Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was CM.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Deputy Chief Minister?
o: The post is not mentioned in the Constitution
A Deputy CM is sworn in as a Minister
He ranks with Union Ministers of State in precedence
The post is created by Article 164(1A)
new.x: The Deputy CM is not mentioned in the Constitution; Article 164(1A) deals with the size of the Council of Ministers.

new.s: The Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 proposes to amend Articles:
new.x: The Bill amends Articles 75, 164 and 239AA to remove a PM, CM or Minister held in custody for 30 consecutive days.

new.s: The Advocate General of a State is appointed under Article:
new.x: Article 165 provides for the Advocate General, the State counterpart of the Attorney General (Art. 76).

new.s: The remuneration of the Advocate General of a State is determined by the:
new.x: The Governor appoints the Advocate General and determines his remuneration, not the Legislature.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Advocate General of a State:
1. He holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
2. He has the right to vote in the State Legislature under Article 177.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Under Article 177 he may speak and take part in proceedings but has no vote.

new.s: To be appointed Advocate General of a State, a person must be qualified to be appointed a:
new.x: The Advocate General must be qualified to be a High Court judge: a citizen with 10 years of judicial office or as an HC advocate.

new.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State?
new.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State; Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was the first CM of united AP (1956).

new.s: In which of the following is the Chief Minister appointed by the President?
new.x: In States the Governor appoints the CM; in Delhi (Art. 239AA) and Puducherry the President appoints the CM.

new.s: The salaries of State ministers are fixed by the State Legislature under Article:
new.x: Article 164(5) leaves salaries to the State Legislature by law; until then the Second Schedule applies.

new.s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
new.x: K. Pratibha Bharati (1999-2004) was the first woman Speaker of the AP Assembly.

new.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2015 raised the strength of the AP Legislative Council from 50 to:
new.x: The 2015 Act raised the AP Council from 50 to 58 (one-third of 175); Telangana's Council has 40.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council, abolished in 1985, was revived in:
new.x: The Council was abolished in 1985 under the NTR government and revived in 2007 under Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Assembly's January 2020 resolution to abolish the Legislative Council was:
o: Struck down by the High Court
new.x: The January 2020 abolition resolution was withdrawn in November 2021, so the AP Council continues.

new.s: When the united Andhra Pradesh Assembly was formed in 1956, its strength was:
new.x: The united AP Assembly of 1956 had 301 members and was unicameral; 294 was the strength split in 2014.

new.s: How many States have a Legislative Council at present (2026)?
new.x: Six States have Councils: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh.

new.s: The Legislative Council of Jammu and Kashmir was abolished in:
new.x: The J&K Council was abolished by the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019; Tamil Nadu abolished its Council in 1986.

new.s: The powers and privileges of members of a State Legislature are dealt with in Article:
new.x: Article 194 covers powers and privileges; Article 208 covers rules of procedure.

new.s: Each House of a State Legislature makes rules to regulate its procedure under Article:
new.x: Article 208 provides for rules of procedure; Article 194 deals with privileges.

new.s: The language to be used in a State Legislature is provided for in Article:
new.x: Article 210 allows Hindi, English or the official language of the State in the Legislature.

new.s: The minimum age for membership of a State Legislative Assembly (25 years) is laid down in Article:
new.x: Article 173 sets the age qualifications (25 for the Assembly, 30 for the Council), not Articles 170 or 171.

new.s: In which of the following elections do the elected MLAs NOT vote?
new.x: Only MPs elect the Vice-President; elected MLAs vote for the President, Rajya Sabha and one-third of the Legislative Council.

new.s: A deadlock between the two Houses of a State Legislature over an ordinary Bill is resolved by:
o: The will of the Assembly, as there is no joint sitting
A joint sitting summoned by the Governor
A joint sitting presided over by the Speaker
new.x: There is no joint sitting in State Legislatures (unlike Art. 108); the Assembly prevails.

new.s: The Speaker's decisions on defection under the Tenth Schedule were held subject to judicial review in:
new.x: Kihoto Hollohan (1992) held the Speaker's Tenth Schedule decisions subject to judicial review.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the State Legislative Assembly:
1. Its strength is not more than 500 and not less than 60.
2. Sikkim, with 32 seats, is an exception to the minimum strength.
3. Its quorum is 10 members or one-tenth of the members, whichever is less.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The quorum is 10 or one-tenth, whichever is greater, not less.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 199(3) – Speaker certifies a Money Bill
new.x: Article 199(3) gives the Speaker the final say on a Money Bill. Article 202 is the Annual Financial Statement, 207 the recommendation, and 197 ordinary Bills.
